content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "Indirect Fire Protection Capability Increment 2 (budget line 8930C61001) is a U.S. Army procurement line funded in the Missile Procurement, Army appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "51f85301c49f060a"}}, {"text": "The Indirect Fire Protection Capability Increment 2 (IFPC Inc 2) is a ground-based weapon system designed to acquire, track, engage, and defeat cruise missiles, unmanned aircraft systems, and rocket, artillery, and mortar threats.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a1a2fd25fe993683"}}, {"text": "The system consists of a launcher and interceptor integrated with the Army Integrated Air and Missile Defense open systems architecture, the IAMD Battle Command System, and the Sentinel sensor, and it is part of the Army Transformation Initiative aligned to the Army's air-and-missile-defense modernization priorities.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a1a2fd25fe993683"}}, {"text": "The Army entered a Middle Tier of Acquisition Rapid Prototyping phase in September 2021, awarding a firm-fixed-price Other Transaction Authority agreement to Dynetics, Inc. to deliver the IFPC Inc 2 prototype solution, and upon completing that phase in April 2025 the program entered Rapid Fielding.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a1a2fd25fe993683"}}, {"text": "The FY 2026 base procurement dollars fund 62 IFPC Inc 2 launchers, 148 AIM-9X missiles, and 24 IFPC magazines, with the increase over FY 2025 driven by higher procurement quantities of launchers, interceptors, and magazines.", "citation": {"fact_id": "33f964f9aa238eb5"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding is $1,018,579 thousand (about $1.02 billion) requested for FY 2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "170ef8af0af3cf09"}}, {"text": "In FY 2024 the program recorded actual spending of $256,753 thousand (about $257 million), so the FY 2026 request is roughly four times its recent execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "76952347a23ba9b2"}}, {"text": "The FY 2026 request splits into a discretionary request of $830,579 thousand (about $831 million) and a reconciliation (mandatory) request of $188,000 thousand (about $188 million).", "citation": {"fact_id": "87dea5a59191828c"}}, {"text": "The $188,000 thousand mandatory portion is the reconciliation piece added to the discretionary base to reach the FY 2026 total.", "citation": {"fact_id": "868624774556b40a"}}, {"text": "Per the program narrative, the mandatory funds procure an additional 284 AIM-9X missiles and associated magazines in FY 2026, with further detail in Section 20003 (Missile Defense) of the Reconciliation Exhibit.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a1a2fd25fe993683"}}, {"text": "The FY 2026 cost of the IFPC Inc 2 Middle Tier of Acquisition Rapid Fielding effort is $951,370 thousand, including research, development, test and evaluation and procurement of mission-essential items.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a1a2fd25fe993683"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Army, with funding drawn from the Missile Procurement, Army appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "4b6b05b22a41a437"}}, {"text": "The prototype solution is delivered by Dynetics, Inc. under a firm-fixed-price Other Transaction Authority agreement awarded during the Middle Tier of Acquisition Rapid Prototyping phase.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a1a2fd25fe993683"}}, {"text": "The system draws on an interim capability path in which the Army, in response to a February 2019 Directed Requirement, procured two interim cruise-missile-defense (Iron Dome Defense System - Army, IDDS-A) batteries, later leased to the Government of Israel beginning in the first quarter of FY 2024.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a1a2fd25fe993683"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
